The skyscraper began with a rope cut on purpose. In New York in 1854, buildings rarely passed 4 floors, because people would not climb more, and nobody trusted an elevator rope.

Elisha Otis, a bedstead mechanic, built a platform that locks if the rope breaks. At the Crystal Palace he rode it high above a crowd while an assistant cut the rope with an axe. The platform dropped 2 feet and stopped. Orders followed, 15 elevators in 1855 and 27 in 1856. In 1857 the first passenger safety elevator went into a New York store. Otis died in 1861, aged 49. Otis says its elevators and escalators now move 2.5 billion people a day.
